actions.findings:
Energy costs for memory erasure are bounded by environmental temperature and non-equilibrium interaction terms. [peer-3d80ce4af7c184d54bcc9333]

Non-reciprocal couplings between system components modulate entropy production in information engines. [peer-f3ee30889b8396e02ea0588a]

Coarse-graining of physical states places lower bounds on retrievable entropy production and predictive information. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]
actions.limitations: Findings assume defined Markovian or overdamped regimes; applicability to complex, high-inertia, or non-Markovian memory architectures remains theoretically constrained.
actions.next_questions: Can the energy cost of maintaining specific reliability levels be mapped to explicit non-reciprocal coupling parameters?
actions.reason: Revision required to integrate new dissipation bounds and non-equilibrium evidence into the memory reliability model.
actions.summary: Memory reliability and retention time are fundamentally limited by energy dissipation. Our revision incorporates findings that non-equilibrium environments and non-reciprocal couplings modulate Landauer erasure costs, establishing that predictive power in information engines is constrained by available energy and coarse-grained state access.
